key_insight: Blackjack uses just two similarity features from cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns to distinguish cancer from healthy samples, including early-stage cancers.
clinical_relevance: This research could support blood-based multi-cancer early detection, rather than drug discovery, but does not establish readiness for clinical screening.
method: Encode DNA sequence context around plasma cfDNA fragmentation sites in position probability matrices.
Measure each sample’s similarity to healthy and cancer reference cohorts.
Use the two similarity features in logistic regression to classify samples.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation on two external whole-genome sequencing datasets achieved a minimum AUC of 0.993 and 91.8% sensitivity at 98% specificity overall; stage I sensitivity was 89.8%.
watch_item: Prospective validation in representative screening populations is needed to establish real-world performance and false-positive burden.
paper_title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
